arguments.literal: `constitution.agent_bootstrap` embeds no other constitution. It names one basis-qualified bootstrap entrypoint and the local instruction files (such as `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` targets) whose small discovery block the manager owns between explicit markers. Each target is a portable relative path resolved against `product.source_project`; absolute paths, parent traversal, redirected path components and escape from that boundary fail closed. A fleet additionally confines every resolved source project to its explicitly authorised fleet root and preflights every target before the first write. Exactly one correctly ordered marker span may be replaced; the bytes before and after it, trailing whitespace included, stay project-owned and byte-identical, and appending a new span preserves all existing bytes as an exact prefix.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION section 4, constitution.agent_bootstrap; P6, P3, P5

`constitution.stdo.source.repository` identifies the transport source. `constitution.stdo.selector` is a mutable `stdo://channels/<version>` discovery selector whose alias semantics are owned by the release law (the RELEASE member). Neither is operative authority. `constitution.stdo.basis.uri` and `constitution.stdo.basis.manifest_sha256` are the sole authored STDO selection for that Product Definition. No cache, registry entry, source checkout, version alias, schema or agent file may silently replace the basis selected in the Product Definition. A project-local exact copy stays lawful when explicitly bound and verified; it is not the default, and file proximity cannot select it.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION sections 4, 12; P6, P3

Tools discover `stdo_*.json` recursively within the selected workspace boundary: definitions at the workspace root and definitions at arbitrarily deep nested project roots. Recursive fleet discovery prunes these exact directory names as version-control, dependency, generated, cache or managed-store internals: `.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.bzr`, `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `site-packages`, `build`, `dist`, `out`, `target`, `.gradle`, `.tox`, `.nox`, `.cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, `__pycache__`, `.genesis` and `.stdo`. A discovered Product Definition may not itself be a symlink. Directory nesting creates no implicit inheritance, ownership, composition or constitutional override.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION sections 4, 9; P3, P5, P6

When bootstrapping a project or repricing a requirement surface: resolve the applicable product definition, verify its exact installed basis, load its declared bootstrap entrypoint (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §12), then load the goals surface or the bound equivalent current work-wave carrier;
SPEC_METHOD section 4 Procedures, the first four steps of the bootstrapping sequence (the sequence continues there); P6
Executive attention is event-driven by default.
EXECUTIVE_BASELINE section 6 Event-driven attention; P0, P2

The bootstrap routes agents to the applicable Product Definition, the exact installed basis and the owning sources; it can neither restate nor override them. README Routes, each row read in order: bind one project to the method: SPEC_METHOD §1, then PRODUCT_DEFINITION. Do a bounded piece of work: ACTIVATION §1–3, REFERENCE_FRAME §11, then SPEC_METHOD §4. Coordinate work as Executive, Worker or Reviewer: EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §3 for direct versus coordinated entry, §6 and §12 for the Executive's duties and the transition, then §16 to adopt or replace it. Resume work someone else left: ACTIVATION §5 and §7, then TICKETS §7. Find the clause that owns a term: GLOSSARY, then PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION section 4; README Routes (rows abridged to their member references); P6, P3, P5
For a requested Product scope exactly one applicable definition is selected; zero or several unresolved definitions fail closed, and a symlinked definition is refused.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION section 9; P6, P5

A derived surface or projected frame carries the path and digest of each deciding source it was derived from, and of each index it watches (GLOSSARY §2). A change to any of those digests makes it stale, and it must be regenerated or explicitly re-accepted before an installation treats it as current. A matching digest establishes identity, not fidelity or sufficiency. The raw owning members of the same selected cut remain the deciding authority and decide when a derived surface or frame is stale or insufficient for a question. Within their declared scope, derived instructions preserve the owning clauses' applicability, obligations, permissions, exclusions, decision owners and invalidators. A summary, bootstrap or index cannot require a stricter or weaker relation by compression.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION section 11 Staleness binding; P3, P5, P6, P4b

A derived surface or projected frame decides standalone only the questions that its own source members own. It refuses to close a question owned by another member, or one that joins the law of several owners; the step returns out_of_frame (§3) naming the owning members, and the question is decided from those members at their current digests or from a derived surface whose declared sources include every owner of it. A prompt is rendered contract over typed authority; it is not source law. Construction starts from the highest live authority surface the question needs. The raw owning members are the fallback when a derived surface or projected frame is stale, missing or insufficient for a named unresolved question.
ACTIVATION section 2 Standalone scope and Prompt construction; P6, P1, P0, P5

`sync` installs and verifies only the exact basis already selected by the Product Definition and never consults its mutable selector; `adopt --dry-run` resolves the annotated selector and immutable RC, and presents the target cut, tag object, commit, tree, manifest digest, current Product-Definition byte digest and a deterministic adoption-plan digest, without mutation; mutating `adopt` requires that exact prior plan digest as explicit acceptance, re-derives it before installation, installs only the bound target, rechecks the Product Definition bytes, and atomically changes only its basis and its basis-relative schema locator; any drift refuses mutation;
PRODUCT_DEFINITION section 4 command boundaries; P6, P5

frame_indexes.scope: Bootstrap: from discovery of a product definition to the exact basis, the derived-surface staleness and scope law, and the first members to load.
